description:
Dolt is a SQL database that you can fork, clone, branch, merge, push and pull just like a git repository.

Dolt is a SQL database that you can fork, clone, branch, merge, push and pull just like a git repository.
Connect to Dolt just like any MySQL database to run queries or update the data using SQL commands.
Use the command line interface to import CSV files, commit your changes, push them to a remote, or merge your teammate's changes.
Merged PRs
dolt
- 12530: Decode each side of kv joins with its own NodeStore
  lookup and merge joins across databases panicked with "empty chunk returned from ChunkStore" when a row had out-of-line values, because the row joiner resolved both sides through a single NodeStore.
  Fixes: #12518
- 12512: Merge convergently added columns that only one side changed
  Merges rows cleanly when both branches add the same column and only one side changes its value.
  Fixes #10909
- 12508: Keep binlog table IDs stable across transactions
  Keep binlog table IDs stable for each exact database and table name, and send a fresh table map with every row transaction. Forward rotation events so CDC readers clear their cached mappings when they catch up across a Dolt restart.
  Fixes #12244
- 12494: reuse hash in archive.ChunkSource.getMany
- 12477: Store and enforce NULLS NOT DISTINCT for unique indexes
  Stores a nulls_not_distinct flag on unique indexes and enforces it on writes, index builds, and merges.
  Companion PRs: dolthub/go-mysql-server#4155, dolthub/doltgresql#3845
- 12476: Convert strict lookup keys of another extended type to the column's type
  Fixes primary key lookups on Doltgres columns compared with a literal of another type by converting the literal to the column's type.
  Companion PR: dolthub/doltgresql#3849
go-mysql-server
- 4175: Log authenticated user and client IP on new SQL connections
  Emit the existing info-level NewConnection event after authentication and session registration. Include the authenticated SQL username and the TCP peer IP alongside the connection ID and multi-statement setting.
  NewConnection now counts authenticated sessions. Rejected credentials continue to produce the existing authentication warning.
- 4173: fix case-sensitive strings in distinct op
  DISTINCT replies on hashing, which requires type information in many cases including strings because of collations.
  fixes: #12502
- 4170: sql/analyzer: scope lookup join NULL matching to the selected equality
  Fix #12505
  Close #4169
- 4163: Support aggregate FILTER clauses
  Supports aggregate FILTER (WHERE ...) clauses set in the vitess AST.
  Companion PRs: dolthub/vitess#508, dolthub/doltgresql#3872
- 4160: fix incorrect scale comparison for rounding decimals
  apd.Decimal stored v.Exponent as a negative value.
- 4157: use stack allocated *apd.Decimal buffer for wire format output
  Adds stack allocated apd.Decimal buffer for writing output to wire format, which avoids extra mallocs.
  benchmarks: #12493 (comment)
- 4156: CVE GO-2026-6612: Upgrade x/net to v0.61.0
- 4155: Add a nulls not distinct option for unique indexes
  Adds an index option that makes unique indexes treat NULLs as equal to each other.
  Companion PRs: #12477, dolthub/doltgresql#3845
- 4152: Hash equal values the same way via a Hashable interface
  Hashes values that compare as equal identically, including times in different locations and slices.
  Companion PR: dolthub/doltgresql#3846
- 4151: Plan fewer foreign keys for UPDATE and DELETE
  Plans only the foreign keys an UPDATE can affect, and skips planning the foreign keys of children that a referential action only restricts.
  Companion PRs: #12470, dolthub/doltgresql#3841
- 4143: Don't implicitly commit statements that read a view
  A statement that reads a view commits the open transaction. A later ROLLBACK no longer undoes writes made before the view was read, other sessions see those writes immediately, and savepoints are lost:
  CREATE TABLE t (id INT PRIMARY KEY);
  CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT * FROM t;
  START TRANSACTION;
  SAVEPOINT s;
  INSERT INTO t VALUES (1);
  SELECT * FROM v;          -- commits the transaction
  RELEASE SAVEPOINT s;      -- ERROR 1105 (HY000): SAVEPOINT s does not exist
  ROLLBACK;
  SELECT * FROM t;          -- returns 1; MySQL returns no rows
  The same happens when the view is read by INSERT ... SELECT, by a subquery in UPDATE or DELETE, or by a multi-table UPDATE. Reading the base table directly doesn't trigger it.
  Cause. resolveView (sql/planbuilder/from.go) binds the view's stored CREATE VIEW statement with the builder of the statement that reads the view. buildDDL sets QFlagDDL on that builder's query flags, which belong to the outer statement. AddTransactionCommittingIter reads QFlagDDL as an implicit commit (sql/rowexec/transaction_iters.go). As a result, TransactionCommittingIter.Close commits the session's transaction and clears it, even when autocommit is off.
  Fix. resolveView restores the outer statement's QFlagDDL after binding the view definition. Reading a view no longer marks the statement as DDL. A real DDL statement that reads a view, such as CREATE VIEW w AS SELECT * FROM v, keeps the flag and still commits implicitly. QFlagDDL is read only by the implicit commit check. Other flags set while binding the view body, such as the subquery and join flags, are left alone.
  Tests.
  - TestViewReferenceDoesNotSetDDLFlag in sql/planbuilder/from_test.go checks the query flags for SELECT, INSERT ... SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE with a view subquery, and a multi-table UPDATE that reads a view. None of them is DDL. CREATE VIEW ... AS SELECT ... FROM v still is. Before the fix, the six non-DDL cases fail.
  - New transaction script queries reading views are not implicitly committed in enginetest/queries/transaction_queries.go. A second client doesn't see the writes after the view reads, RELEASE SAVEPOINT still works, and ROLLBACK undoes both the INSERT and the INSERT ... SELECT from the view. The memory harness skips transaction scripts with setup statements, so this one runs in Dolt's TestTransactions and TestTransactionsPrepared. With this branch replaced into Dolt, the script fails five assertions before the fix and passes after it.
    Fixes #12236
- 4135: Fix MIN and MAX nullability in CREATE TABLE AS SELECT
  MIN and MAX can return NULL for a group containing only NULL values or for empty input, but their generated expressions marked the result as non-nullable, causing CREATE TABLE AS SELECT to fail
  Declare both aggregates nullable in the generator, add a CTAS regression for both cases, and refresh existing schema and plan expectations
  Fixes #12385
vitess
- 508: Add Filter to aggregate expression nodes
  Adds a Filter field for aggregate FILTER (WHERE ...) clauses to FuncExpr, GroupConcatExpr and OrderedInjectedExpr.
  Companion PRs: dolthub/go-mysql-server#4163, dolthub/doltgresql#3872
- 506: sqlparser: accept boolean expressions in generated columns
  Accept full expressions in generated-column definitions so AS (value < 8) works without an extra pair of parentheses. Preserve the outer ParenExpr needed for DDL formatting and the original regression coverage across CREATE/ALTER, abbreviated/full syntax, and virtual/stored columns.
  Supersedes dolthub/vitess#503 by @sciyoshi, preserving the original commit authorship. Applied on current main and regenerated sql.go to resolve the generated-parser merge conflict.
  The full sqlparser test suite and tools/check_make_parser.sh pass. Parser generation reports zero shift/reduce and zero reduce/reduce conflicts.
  Fixes #12343.
